  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Parks & Recreation Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are
committed to the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter
and spirit of Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private
life. We will be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest. We
will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality
and integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain
from abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions in which
we have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create
a perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest
in thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to any
other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or censure
of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established .

Staff Recommendation:

That the Parks and Recreation Commission provide input regarding the Irwindale Cheer
program .

Background and Analysis:

The Irwindale Recreation Department offers the Irwindale Cheer Program annually over
a period of nine months. The 2019-2020 Cheer season was suspended due to the
COVID-19 Pandemic. Each team was able to compete in two competitions prior to the
suspension. In August of this year, two 8 week Virtual Camps were offered, one for
Munchkin Cheer and one for Competition Cheer. Fifteen cheerleaders participated in
these virtual programs, which were open to residents and non-residents.

As we look into the future of the Irwindale Cheer program , we offer the following options
for your consideration:

  Option 1: Continue to offer virtual Cheer program
  Option 2: Offer outdoor Cheer program
  Option 3: Offer virtual Cheer program in the winter and begin outdoor Cheer
  program in the spring.

Option 1
Offer two additional virtual camps beginning in January and running for eight weeks. One
camp will be offered for Munchkin Cheer (ages 4 - 6) and one for Competition Cheer
(ages 7 - 13).

Option 2
Should the Parks and Recreation Commission recommend an in person cheer program ,
we will do so in full compliance with the LA County Health guidelines requiring , but is not
limited to the following :

  1. Limit registration to ensure social distancing protocols. 8ft social distancing is
  required for any type of outdoor physical activity.

  required to bring their own gear (face covering, water bottle, yoga mat or
  towel).
  2.  Program must be offered outside only.
  3.  Person to person contact is prohibited .
  4.  No routines or stunting is permitted, conditioning only.

  IR\VINDALE  Item No. 2C
  AGENDA REPORT  December 2, 2020

 Date:  December 2, 2020
 To:  Honorable Chairman & Park and Recreation Commission Board Members
 From:  Theresa Olivares, Assistant City Manager
 Issue:  Irwindale Park Improvements Phase Ill Update

Assistant City Manager's Recommendation:

Receive and file the update on the Irwindale Park Improvements Phase Ill.

Administrative Action:
 Prepared, Submitted, and Approved by:

 Theresa Olivares, Assistant City Manager
 (626) 430-2294

Background:

Since the last update on November 4, 2020, relating to the City of Irwindale Park
Improvements Phase Ill (Project), the contractor has completed several elements. The
complete items include landscape planting and sod, bus shelter and walkway roofing ,
asphalt paving, installation of concrete tables, benches, and trash cans. Staff anticipates
the light poles for the entire project and the light fixtures for the shelter walkway to be
delivered on December 4, 2020 and the remaining memorial pavers will be installed after
they have been received . The basketball court stripping will be completed by the third
week December. In order to ensure the public's safety, the Project area cannot be
opened to the public until all lights are installed and operational.

Additionally, on November 4, 2020, the Park and Recreation Commission recommended
that staff contact the applicants who purchased a memorial garden paver and allow them
to submit a 2-minute video dedication to honor their loved one(s). Notices were mailed
to the applicants on November 18, 2020, advising them of the purpose, time limit, and
December 8, 2020 submission deadline. Applicants requiring assistance were advised
to contact Ms. Iris Espino to set up an appointment.

This staff report will be supplemented by a photo slideshow of the Project.

Fiscal Impact:
None
